## What This Project Is

**Netclaw-Miles** is a production-grade AI network engineering agent built on the OpenClaw framework (Node.js) with Claude (claude-opus-4-6) as the AI backbone. The agent's persona is "Miles" — a CCIE R&S #AI-001 coworker with 15 years of network engineering experience, specialized in Cisco Meraki and enterprise networking.

The agent operates as an autonomous network engineer: it reads its own identity (SOUL.md), the user's profile (USER.md), and the local infrastructure map (TOOLS.md) at startup, then begins an immutable GAIT (Git Audit Trail) session before taking any action.

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| AI Framework | OpenClaw (Node.js, npm global) |
| AI Model | Anthropic Claude (opus-4-6 primary, sonnet-4-6 fallback) |
| Skill Delivery | OpenClaw workspace (~/.openclaw/workspace) |
| Tool Integration | MCP (Model Context Protocol) — stdio/HTTP |
| Device Automation | Meraki Dashboard API + Meraki MCP (~804 endpoints) |
| Protocol Participation | Custom protocol-mcp (Python 3 — Scapy, FastMCP) |
| Config/Secrets | .env file (not in repo) |
| Audit Trail | GAIT MCP — every session Git-committed |
| Install Automation | Bash (install.sh + setup.sh) |

## Deployment Model

- **Not containerized** — runs as a local process via OpenClaw CLI
- **Single-user** by default — USER.md customized per person, multi-agent via AGENTS.md
- **Credentials** — stored in `~/.openclaw/.env` (written by setup.sh), never in repo
- **Skills** — deployed to `~/.openclaw/workspace` (outside repo)
- **MCP servers** — cloned/installed to `~/mcp-servers/` (outside repo, gitignored)

---

## Agent Identity & Operational Rules

Miles follows hard rules from SOUL.md:
1. Always run `show` before any config change
2. Always create a ServiceNow CR (except in lab mode)
3. Always commit to GAIT before and after changes
4. Always verify after changes
5. Never run destructive commands (write erase, reload, delete, format)
6. Never auto-quarantine endpoints — human confirmation required
7. Never exfiltrate sensitive data
8. Ask before external communications (Slack, email, tickets)
9. Self-update knowledge files immediately when learning something new
